RE:              December 18, 2025, Open Meeting, Agenda Item No. 13
                 Project No. 58777, Triennial Reliability Assessment for the ERCOT Region under
                 §25.508
                 Staff Recommendations for 2026 Reliability Standard Assessment


In this memorandum, Commission Staff proposes a roadmap, with dates and major milestones, for
the Commission’s first triennial assessment of the Commission’s reliability standard.
Additionally, Staff highlights a few important policy issues about which the Commission may
wish to provide guidance to assist with framing the assessment properly.

According to Commission rules, beginning January 1, 2026, ERCOT must initiate an assessment
to determine whether the bulk power system for the ERCOT region is meeting the reliability
standard and is likely to continue to meet the reliability standard for the following three years. 1
The rule also lays out a process for Commission review and determination.

Staff’s proposed roadmap adheres to the rule’s requirements and suggests expectations for Staff,
ERCOT, the Independent Market Monitor (IMM), industry stakeholders, and other interested
members of the public to participate in this first triennial reliability standard assessment. Staff’s
proposal is designed to complete a technically rigorous and complex evaluation of the
Commission’s reliability standard and ensure robust participation from external stakeholders. As
a result, Staff anticipates needing the better part of an entire calendar year to complete the full
assessment.

Staff looks forward to reviewing this proposal with you during the December 18, 2025 open
meeting.

B) SIGNIFICANT POLICY ITEMS
1) Reevaluating the Cost of New Entry (CONE)

During its July 31, 2024 open meeting, the Commission adopted a CONE value of $140,000/MW-
year that would apply to ERCOT’s planning studies. Since then, changes to assumptions that serve
as the foundation to calculate CONE may have impacted the reasonableness of this value, such as
supply chain constraints and inflation. To assess the need for revising the CONE value for the
2026 assessment, ERCOT held a workshop on November 21, 2025. In that workshop, Brattle
Group and Sargent & Lundy presented their findings from the PJM 2025 CONE Study 5 and
provided insights from a generation market supply chain and equipment cost outlook. The new
CONE, as calculated by Brattle for PJM, showed a 31% increase over the prior CONE. This new
PJM CONE value adjusted for inflation is about $206,000/MW-year. (in 2026 dollars).

ERCOT Staff recommended to request stakeholder comments on the topics discussed at the
workshop and then to work with the Brattle/Sargent & Lundy team on developing a CONE update
proposal to be filed with the Commission on January 15, 2026 (concurrent with the modeling

assumptions filing). The proposal would likely be based on a “streamlined” study approach, which
would leverage the PJM CONE study results. It will be an update rather than a brand-new bottom-
up CONE Study. The proposed study would include an estimation of the maximum MW capacity
amounts of the reference technologies expected to be available for the 2029 simulation year. These
estimates would consider supply chain issues and be used to develop constraints for capacity
expansion optimization modeling to support market design option analysis. Stakeholders would
have another opportunity to file formal comments in response to ERCOT’s CONE update proposal
alongside their comments on the modeling assumptions.

Staff recommendation: Staff supports ERCOT’s recommendation, as a robust CONE value based
on up-to-date information is essential to evaluate any market design changes that could be
considered by the Commission later next year.


2) Dispatchable Reliability Reserve Service (DRRS)

In Project No. 55845, Review of Ancillary Services in the ERCOT Market, the Commission issued
the following finding:

    TOPIC 6: DISPATCHABLE RELIABILITY RESERVE SERVICE (DRRS)
    Finding – DRRS is one of the tools in the market design toolbox that may assist in meeting the
    ERCOT reliability standard and need not be specially designated as a tool for resource
    adequacy to be utilized for this purpose in the future.

    Next Steps – ERCOT should design DRRS to ensure that it meets its primary role as an
    ancillary service to mitigate operational risks in real time and reduce the use of Reliability
    Unit Commitment. ERCOT should also design flexibility into the mechanism for procuring
    DRRS so that, if the Commission determines that the price for or quantity of DRRS should
    be modified in the future to provide targeted additional generator revenue, this could be
    done without requiring significant additional system changes and without creating artificial
    scarcity or other detrimental effects on the market. ERCOT and stakeholders may have
    additional ideas to achieve this outcome that merit continued examination.

In response to this finding, on November 20, 2025, ERCOT filed NPRR 1310 Dispatchable
Reliability Reserve Service Plus Energy Storage Resource Participation and Release Factor. This
NPRR includes the concept of a Release Factor, which facilities procurement of DRRS in amounts
above what is strictly necessary to mitigate operational risks. However, unless the Commission
determines to procure DRRS in quantities beyond those minimally required to serve operational
uncertainty and concurrently directs ERCOT to establish an appropriate Release Factor, the DRRS
Release Factor will be set to zero. Based on the impact analysis ERCOT provided, implementation
will take 20-30 months after Commission approval.

Staff recommendation: Staff recommends that determination of this parameter be included in the
scope of the 2026 assessment as a possible market design change if the assessment shows that
ERCOT Region is not meeting the reliability standard. Although some of the details are still
pending, ERCOT and stakeholders, while working on the NPRR 1310, could evaluate how a
Release Factor concept could be used to address resource adequacy generally to facilitate the
 Project No. 58777                             Staff’s Roadmap                                    Page 5 of 6


Commission’s determination of an appropriate value, if the Release Factor is ever changed from
its initial value of zero. To facilitate this, the Commission can also ask for feedback on the Aurora
Energy Research Report filed in Project No. 55797. 6 Staff recommends stakeholders and ERCOT
keep NPRR 1309 and NPRR 1310 on concurrent review pathways so that the Commission can use
stakeholder feedback earlier in this reliability standard assessment process. At the December 10,
2025 Protocol Revision Subcommittee meeting, NPRR 1310 was granted urgent status, which Staff
contends is appropriate to make this outcome more likely to be achieved.

In addition, the Commission should consider whether Energy Storage Resources (ESRs) should
be eligible to provide DRRS as an ancillary service. At present, ESR participation is included
within NPRR 1310 in addition to the Release Factor. Staff contends that the Release Factor and
ESR participation are distinct issues that would benefit from separate consideration. If the
Commission agrees, it may want to express that view so that ERCOT and stakeholders can take
appropriate action, if they so choose.


3) Other Possible Market Design Changes, if Needed

ERCOT has operated an energy-only market since its inception and, as such, relies on effective
shortage pricing mechanisms to incent sufficient investment to maintain resource adequacy. The
following are the primary, existing market mechanisms the Commission could adjust if it
determined a market design change were merited by the results of the reliability standard
assessment. Some of these are described in Commission rules and would require rulemakings to
change, while others are described in the ERCOT protocols and may be addressed through the
stakeholder process with appropriate Commission guidance, subject to compliance with PURA
§ 39.1514.

options earlier in the reliability standard assessment process so that stakeholders can have an
opportunity to opine on and the Commission can efficiently and effectively implement any desired
changes, if needed. This can be achieved by gathering stakeholder feedback while ERCOT is
running the simulations between May and late August of 2026.
